title: How many children march in the parade, counted two ways?
description: Scouts march in four rows of five and guides in three rows of five. The children are counted group by group, and again by adding the rows first and multiplying by five. Keeko doubts that five times four plus three counts every child.
teaching_notes: One idea: when rows have the same number in each, add the rows first, so a sum in a bracket is multiplied by the common number. Watch for students who think five times four plus three means five times seven.

source: In a parade, 4 rows of 5 scouts march beside 3 rows of 5 guides.
video_script.why: A learner sees that adding the rows first and multiplying by the row size gives the same count as counting each group.
video_script.substitution: Replace four and three with any numbers of rows and the five with any row size.
video_script.anchor: the Republic Day parade of the book, four rows of five scouts beside three rows of five guides
video_script.wrong_answer: five times four plus three counts all the children
video_script.wrong_move: reads 5 × 4 + 3 as five times seven, so the 5 is thought to reach the 3 as well
video_script.payoff_line: There are thirty five scouts and guides in the parade.

final_answer.spoken: thirty five scouts and guides march, while the slip gives twenty three

video_script.design: One drawing of the parade: four rows of five scouts in one colour beside three rows of five guides in a second colour. The rows join into seven rows of five.

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about a Republic Day parade.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>The boy scouts march in four rows with five scouts in each row.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>The girl guides march in three rows with five guides in each row.
<bookmark mark='h4'/>How many scouts and guides are marching in all?

<bookmark mark='g2'/>Four rows of five scouts are four groups of five.

<bookmark mark='gv2'/>The guides march in three rows of five.

beats.on_screen: To find: scouts and guides together, in two ways; why 5 × 4 + 3 is different

marks.fd2: the slip 5 × 4 + 3 is written to compare later

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to find all the scouts and guides in two ways.
<bookmark mark='fd2'/>We also have to say why five times four plus three is different.

marks.s11: the two group counts are written

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, count each group, and then add.
The scouts are four times five and the guides are three times five.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>The total is four times five plus three times five, which is twenty plus fifteen.

marks.s21: the rows of both groups join into one block

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, add the rows first, because every row holds five.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>The rows are four plus three, and each row has five.
<bookmark mark='s23'/>The total is open bracket four plus three close bracket times five, which is seven times five.

beats.on_screen: 4 × 5 + 3 × 5 = (4 + 3) × 5, the same children counted two ways

marks.s31: the two expressions are joined by an equals sign
marks.s32: both sides are read aloud in order

narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, join the two ways, because they count the same children.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>Four times five plus three times five equals open bracket four plus three close bracket times five.

beats.on_screen: the slip: 5 × 4 + 3 = 20 + 3 = 23; the 5 multiplies only the 4

marks.s41: the slip is written under the bracket form
marks.s42: the 5 is shown reaching only the 4

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, look at five times four plus three.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>The five multiplies only the four, so we get twenty plus three.
<bookmark mark='s43'/>That is only twenty three, so it is a different expression.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 20 + 15 = 35 and 7 × 5 = 35, so 35 scouts and guides march; 5 × 4 + 3 = 23

marks.a2: 23 is shown as a different number

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>There are thirty five scouts and guides in the parade.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Both ways give thirty five, but the slip gives twenty three.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 5 × 4 + 3; the bubble is struck out and the guide rows are shown needing three full rows of five

narration: <bookmark mark='k2'/>Keeko thinks five times four plus three counts all the children.
<bookmark mark='k3'/>But the five multiplies only the four there.
<bookmark mark='k4'/>The guides need three full rows of five too.
